intro: Minnesota runs its elections through county auditors and city and township clerks.

id_rule.text: If you register on Election Day, you must show proof of where you live. You can show a Minnesota driver's license or ID card, another document approved by the Secretary of State, or a student fee statement with a photo ID. A registered voter from your precinct can also sign an oath to vouch for you.

check.text: Minnesota Secretary of State voter information.
check.label: Elections and voting

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Absentee and early voting in person
dates.detail: You can vote an absentee ballot in person at your county elections office starting 46 days before Election Day, through Monday, Nov. 2. Counties and cities set their own sites and hours, so call before you go. Any voter can vote early by mail for any reason.

dates.label: Last day to register before Election Day
dates.detail: You cannot register by the usual methods during the 20 days before Election Day, so this is the last day (21 days before). Minnesota has same-day registration: you can also register at your polling place on Election Day with proof of where you live.

dates.label: Absentee ballot application deadline
dates.detail: You can apply for an absentee ballot up to one day before Election Day. Apply sooner if you want the ballot mailed to you.

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 8 pm. A mailed absentee ballot must arrive by 8 pm. If you hand-deliver it to your county auditor or city clerk, it must be there by 5 pm.
